title: Rays make Danielle Dockx one of MLB’s highest-ranking front-office women
content:
The Tampa Bay Rays promoted Danielle Dockx on Monday to senior director of player development, making her one of the first women to lead a farm system for any of the 30 major-league teams and one of the highest-ranking women in any MLB front office.

According to a team release, Dockx will oversee the Rays’ day-to-day player development process, collaborating with the organization’s player development leadership group to create a structured environment that allows for consistent growth and development of minor-league players and staff.

“Dani has been an integral part of our player development department for several years now, taking on more of a leadership role this past season,” Rays vice president and assistant general manager Kevin Ibach said in a statement.

Dockx began working for the Rays as a baseball operations fellow in 2018 before rising through the organization to serve as the Rays’ director of player programs and integration the past two seasons. The Rays are widely regarded as having one of baseball’s best farm systems and player development operations.

Dockx is among a small group of women who have held such a high-ranking baseball position. Sara Goodrum served as the Houston Astros’ director of player development from 2021 to 2023, making her the majors’ first female farm director. She currently works as director of special projects for the Miami Marlins, whose director of player development is Rachel Balkovec.

Chanda Lawdermilk is a vice president and assistant general manager with the Rays, and Sammi Bireley serves as their director of baseball operations.

Jean Afterman has served as an assistant general manager for the New York Yankees since 2001. Alyssa Nakken is the director of player development for the Cleveland Guardians’ player development operation at their extended spring training complex in Arizona. Eve Rosenbaum, Raquel Ferreira and Sarah Gelles serve as assistant general managers for the Baltimore Orioles, Boston Red Sox and Pittsburgh Pirates, respectively.
